text:
Maya: heads-up — ran the HF->Redwood generation_config mapping on the new llama-ish checkpoint and saw a reproducible quality regression in our chat evals. seems tied to repetition_penalty mapping and token aliasing. anyone seen this?
Jun: can you paste the HF generation_config you started from and the mapped output? small snippet is fine.
Maya: sure — original HF bits: ```json
{
  "temperature": 0.8,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "top_k": 40,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.2,
  "max_new_tokens": 256
}
``` mapped by our script -> this ended up as: ```json
{
  "temperature": 0.8,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "top_k": 40,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.2,
  "max_new_tokens": 256,
  "_applied_special_token_filter": true
}
``` but evals show more repetitive completions than HF baseline.
Carlos: odd — that mapping looks identity-ish. two quick suspects: 1) tokenization differences (special token aliases causing repeated token ids), 2) we accidentally apply rep-penalty both in the sampling phase and again in an extra post-filter.
Priya: do you have a sample prompt + produced generations (baseline vs post-mapping)? small 2-line example is enough.
Maya: yes. prompt: ```
System: You are a helpful assistant.
User: List 5 pizza toppings.
``` baseline HF output (gen from HF-run): "1. Pepperoni
2. Mushrooms
3. Onions
4. Sausage
5. Olives" mapped -> our Redwood-run: "1. Pepperoni
2. Pepperoni
3. Mushrooms
4. Onions
5. Olives" — notice the duplicate early.
Jun: that smells like repetition_penalty interacting with token boundaries. if the tokenizer emits a special alias token (eg "<|start|>") that is present in the context but gets filtered inconsistently, the rep-penalty scoring vector can treat the next token as new and overweight prev token tokens. also: older conversion code treats top_k=0 and top_k=None as different semantics.
Carlos: find: the tokenizer for this model maps both "User:" and "User: \n" to two different token sequences (aliasing). when we compute last-token history for rep-penalty we used raw token ids from the model output but for candidate scoring we canonicalize special tokens — mismatch. result: the last emitted visible token isn't considered, so penalty not applied to the immediate repeat.
Priya: actionable mapping rules proposal: 1) canonicalize special tokens in both history and candidate ids before computing rep-penalty, 2) clamp repetition_penalty to >= 1.0 (no <1), 3) interpret top_k: if given 0 -> treat as unlimited (None) to match HF, 4) map null/absent top_p -> default 1.0 rather than 0.0, 5) ensure temperature is parsed as float always (avoid int coercion).
Maya: +1 on tests. I also noticed quantized int8 runs amplify the effect — sampling noise is lower so rep-penalty bug becomes visible.
infra-bot: deploy-log: hf-conversion v3.7.1 -> hf-to-rw mapper updated 2026-03-19 21:10 UTC (sha: a1b2c3). rolling.
Jun: small repro command I used locally (linux): ```bash
python -m rw_eval.run_gen --model /mnt/models/llama-x --prompt-file examples/pizza.txt --generation-config hf_gen.json --map-hf-to-rw --seed 42 --quantize none
``` compare with `--quantize int8` to see amplification.
Carlos: added a tiny patch in my branch that canonicalizes tokens in `hf_conversion.repetition_history()` — sanity unit included. diff is one-liner conceptually: `history = [tok for tok in tokenizer.normalize_ids(history)]` before scoring.
Priya: can we also add a golden test case to the eval harness that fails if any duplicate appears in first 10 items for a simple enumerative prompt? makes this regression easy to catch.
Maya: that would be great. eval-bot — do we have historical numbers for this model across the chat-listing metric?
Eval-bot: baseline (HF native): Exact-listing-uniqueness@5 = 0.98; Redwood-mapped (before fix): Exact-listing-uniqueness@5 = 0.86; after Carlos' canonicalization patch (local): 0.97. full logs: https://internal.redwood/reports/1895432100/rep-penalty-debug (private).
Jun: next steps: 1) land canonicalization patch, 2) update hf->rw mapping docs to include the rules Priya listed, 3) add unit+eval tests, 4) do a canary on dedicated infra (low RPS). I'll pick up #1 and #3.
Maya: thanks. can someone add a short note in the model onboarding checklist about "verify rep-penalty by enumerative prompts"? saved us time.
Carlos: putting a quick PR description in #eng-releases and pinging QA.
Priya: I'll update the conversion docs and add the top_k/top_p mapping table. also adding a note: treat `generation_config` fields as optional and prefer explicit override in Redwood model config.
Maya: awesome — closing the loop here. feel free to DM if you need sample eval sets. :thumbsup:
Jun: thanks all. I'll watch the canary and post results. :eyes:
